key_insight: A multi-modal temporal attention model using welding images and sound can detect hard-to-see fillet-joint defects in real time with very high accuracy while providing interpretable defect cues.
engineering_relevance: This approach can improve in-process quality control for gas metal arc welding, helping reduce scrap, rework, and post-weld inspection delays.
method: Trained a deep learning defect detector on synchronized welding images and acoustic data from an industrial collaborative welding robot.
Used a temporal attention module to focus on the most informative time windows and improve defect classification.
Applied explainable AI to identify important regions in images and spectrograms and to compare which modality best detects each defect.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the attention module raised the F1 score to 0.99 on internal defect detection tasks including porosity, lack of penetration/fusion, undercut, and cold lap.
watch_item: Performance is reported from collected industrial data, so broader validation across different weld geometries, materials, and shop-floor noise conditions is still needed.
paper_title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
